scope: A disposable Kubernetes v1.36.1 Kind cluster uses synthetic public-model metadata and fixed inert model-like JSON specimens. The pinned YARA-X engine evaluates a local marker rule offline. Bundled kindnet is checked ready. The case applies a restricted quarantine namespace and default-deny ingress/egress NetworkPolicy, then proves its egress effect against two case-owned marker-only listeners with one exact allow exception and an unaffected comparator. It then uses the built-in Pod Security Admission controller and a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to reject nonconforming pods and release pods whose clean-scan decision or exact metadata digest does not match. A narrowly bound ServiceAccount creates the positive release pod through the Kubernetes API; an additional tokenless restricted Job reads a fixed inert model-like JSON fixture, checks only its approved format and fixed marker policy, hashes the exact bytes, and binds the observed hash to the native release ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. A different ServiceAccount is denied. Synthetic offline decision records exercise malware, unsafe-format, embedded-content, missing, and subject-mismatch decisions. This verifies the fixture policy, Kubernetes admission, API authorization, and exact metadata-digest readback. The marker comparison establishes the YARA-X rule behavior for these inert JSON specimens. Real model contents, scanner coverage, the adopted CNI, source authenticity, behavioral safety, production promotion and durable audit storage need deployment evidence. A scoped update identity also verifies that native release admission preserves the exact scanned digest after creation.
